title: Recharge a 400 mL spring wound-drain reservoir and seal its spout plug
instruction: Re-activate the wound drain so that it stays compressed flat on the mat after you let go, with its tethered plug seated in the pouring spout.
context: Done by: registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00; 3,465,400 US workers in 2025) and licensed practical nurses (29-2061.00; 666,900), per O*NET OnLine (BLS 2025 employment data), whose listed work includes monitoring patients after surgery and dressing wounds. Emptying a spring closed-wound suction drain (closed-wound suction drainage reservoir) is routine post-operative ward care. Mosby's nursing procedure: put the device on a flat surface, press down until the top and bottom surfaces touch, then immediately replace the plug. Plugged while expanded, it gives no suction and fluid collects in the wound; the instruction names only the end state. One hand must hold the reservoir flat against about 13 N of spring force while the other picks a small plug and seats it in the spout, so the hold has to last until the seal is made.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Mat, fixed: grey dimpled absorbent bench pad, 26.0 x 22.0 x 0.3 cm, centred at (28.5, 4.0). Wound-drain reservoir, loose: 400 mL 3-spring closed-wound suction unit (145 g dry, 11.2 cm diameter, 7.6 cm tall expanded, 2.0 cm compressed; white polypropylene top and bottom discs, green lid print, clear collapsible film side wall, three internal steel springs, +y inlet port with a short tubing stub, -x finger-press lug, flared pouring spout 15.6 mm ID x 14 mm tall on the +x rim, and an open-sided plug-holder cradle reaching (+7.7, -4.0) cm from its centre) standing upright at (28.0, 5.0) on the mat, fully expanded. Tethered spout plug, loose: 10 g LDPE/PP stopper (1.04 cm tapered stem x 1.25 cm, 2.7 cm blue flange, 2.0 x 0.6 x 1.5 cm blue pull-tab) standing open in the plug-holder cradle at (35.7, 1.0). Visual-only bench props, no collision, behind the work area and not touched by the demo, all beyond x = 42 cm: stainless kidney dish, folded surgical drape, nitrile glove box, disinfectant spray bottle, specimen bag and a disposable syringe.
scoring: Measured with a ruler, a protractor and a side-view video. 0.3: the reservoir is 2.28 cm tall or less (30% of its 7.6 cm expanded height) now, or was pressed to that height at some moment while upright (tilt 18 degrees or less) and resting on the mat (its base less than 1.2 cm above it). 0.7: in addition, the plug now sits in the pouring spout with its flange on the rim (within 6.5 mm sideways, 4.5 mm in height and 22 degrees of the reservoir's own axis). 1.0: in addition, the reservoir is still 2.28 cm tall or less, reservoir and plug show no visible motion (under 1 cm/s), and the tool-centre point between each gripper's finger pads has stayed outside a box 5 cm larger on every side than the reservoir's and the plug's bounding boxes for 4 s; a successful run ends after this has held 1 s more (5 s in all). 0: never pressed flat; the plug was put into the spout while the reservoir was taller than 2.28 cm; at any time the reservoir was lifted more than 2.5 cm off the mat; at the end the reservoir is tipped more than 18 degrees, its centre is more than 2 cm beyond the mat edge, or the reservoir or plug lies more than 5 mm below the table top. Possible: 0, 0.3, 0.7, 1.0.
reset_notes: Unseat the plug and return it upright to the plug-holder cradle at (35.7, 1.0); allow the three reservoir springs to expand fully to 7.6 cm at (28.0, 5.0) on the mat.
fidelity: Three springs: two series slide joints (480 N/m each, 13.4 N flat; chosen, likely below a real unit). Vacuum: spring joints held where they are when the plug seats, released if it unseats. 4 cm tether not simulated (loose plug). Cradle, pull-tab, press lug are gripper aids. Empty, no fluid; outer size estimated. At real size the 27 mm plug is ~24 px at 1280x704 and the middle slide hides under the top plate; proxy: SUBACTION_END log, end close-ups, top plate down + plug in rim.
